payload.name: Include State Memories for Action Questions
payload.description: When a question asks what someone did or did for someone/something, include memory kind 'state' in searches because completed actions may be stored as state memories (e.g., purchases, new possessions, resulting conditions).
content: When a question asks what a person did or what action they took, do not restrict retrieval to event and plan memory kinds; also include state (and profile/preference when relevant), because completed actions are often recorded as state memories (e.g., 'purchased X', 'got new Y', 'has Z').

After the first search, if no event/plan memory clearly answers the action, run a follow-up search using the same subject and action paraphrases (e.g., 'bought', 'got', 'purchased', 'provided', 'gave') without the event/plan filter, and include state kind.
Stop once a memory explicitly states the action or its resulting state is found; do not answer with unrelated activities just because they mention the same subject.

solves: When a question asks what someone did or what action they took, restricting retrieval to event or plan memories can miss the answer when the completed action is stored as a state memory (e.g., a purchase, a new possession, or a resulting condition). The agent should include state memories in such searches and run follow-up queries without the event/plan filter before answering.
